## What was built

**Primitives** — [integer.mbt](integer.mbt): RFC 7541 §5.1 prefixed integers, minimal encodings, `Int64` accumulation with a 2³¹−1 limit, `UnexpectedEof` inside an integer and `IntegerOverflow` for values (or encodings longer than five continuation octets) above the limit. [huffman.mbt](huffman.mbt): the full 257-symbol code, encoded MSB-first with all-ones EOS padding, and decoded without a tree via the canonical property — three table lookups per bit, with the three §5.2 violations (EOS in data, >7 bits of padding, padding not all ones) raising `InvalidHuffman`. [huffman_table.mbt](huffman_table.mbt) is **generated** from Appendix B by a parsing script that verifies the Kraft sum is exactly 2³⁰, prefix-freeness, and canonical ordering.

**Tables** — [static_table.mbt](static_table.mbt) holds Appendix A's 61 entries (cross-checked against the RFC text programmatically); [dynamic_table.mbt](dynamic_table.mbt) keeps entries newest-first with exact `name + value + 32` accounting, eviction on insert and on size change, and the "entry larger than the table empties it and is not inserted" rule.

**Decoder** ([decoder.mbt](decoder.mbt)) — one loop dispatching on the high bits into all five representations, a single `entry_at` for the combined address space (index 0 and past-the-end → `InvalidIndex`), size updates legal only before the first field and only up to the protocol limit, names resolved before the insertion that may evict them.

**Encoder** ([encoder.mbt](encoder.mbt)) — the deterministic greedy strategy (exact → name → literal, always inserting), both literal forms, the two single-field forms, and §4.2 size signalling (smallest requested size, then the final size).

`parse` is a single forward pass over physical lines (blank / comment / header / entry), where an entry may consume several lines through continuation markers. Each line becomes an `Array[Char]` so scanning indexes Unicode scalar values, never UTF-16 code units. Storing into `Doc.global`/`Doc.sections` maps gives last-wins for duplicate keys and re-opening for repeated headers.

Key rules implemented: first `=`/`:` separator wins; trimming of keys/separators/unquoted values; inline `;`/`#` only after whitespace and only on the introducing line; the three per-carrier escape tables (unknown escapes stay literal, so `C:\Program` survives); odd/even trailing-backslash-run continuation with the run-length table; quoted values closed on the same line with only whitespace/comment after; section-name quote unwrapping; control-character and empty-key/section rejection. `print` writes every value double-quoted with `\\ \" \n \r \t` escaped, and wraps a section name in quotes only when it would otherwise be trimmed or wrongly unwrapped.

## Judgment calls where the spec leaves room

- Continuation lines contribute text, so their `;`/`#` stay in the value (the spec says this explicitly in both `ini_spec.mbt` and `specs/ini.md`); only the introducing line is comment-scanned.
- Continuation parity is decided after that comment is removed — a comment runs to end of line, so a backslash behind one is not a marker.
- A trailing run must be at the very end of the line: `k=a\` followed by spaces is a literal backslash, not a marker.
- `[section] ; note` is accepted (only whitespace/comment after `]`), while `[section] junk` is rejected.
- Trimming and gap/comment detection share one whitespace class (`Char::is_whitespace`).
- `print` wraps a section name in quotes when it has edge whitespace or already looks quoted, so those names round-trip; keys have no quoting mechanism, so keys with edge whitespace or separators are documented as outside the printable subset.

Key design points:
- Single-pass recursive-descent parser, no AST: statements are applied immediately to a mutable table tree.
- Five table kinds (root/implicit/header/dotted/inline) encode TOML's rules: one header per table, dotted-key/header conflicts, closed inline tables, static arrays vs. arrays of tables, parent-before-child ordering.
- Chunk-based string scanning preserves non-ASCII/surrogate pairs losslessly; escapes are the only character-level path.
- Floats: since the standard decimal parser aborts on overflow, the parser computes the leading-digit decimal exponent and compares against the exact decimal expansion of `2^1024 − 2^970` (stored as a string), so `1e309 → inf`, `T−1 → max_value`, `T → inf`, huge exponents/mantissas never crash.
- `print` emits one `key = value` line per root entry with nested tables inline, which round-trips for every well-formed document; floats/floats-of-zero/inf/nan and all date-time forms are formatted explicitly.

### Parser behaviour (spec-driven, not fixture-driven)
- Terminators LF / CRLF (one terminator) / lone CR; terminator at EOF allowed; embedded CRLF inside quotes preserved verbatim.

## Key semantics implemented

- **Lines**: LF and CRLF; a trailing newline never creates an extra empty line (which is what makes "continuation marker at EOF" an error).
- **Sections**: `[name]` only, no nested `[`, unclosed/empty/whitespace-only names rejected; quote pair stripped when it wraps the whole name (`[remote "origin"]` keeps its interior quotes); trailing comment allowed, other trailing text rejected; headers register the section immediately (empty sections exist) and re-open on repeat.
- **Entries**: first `=` or `:` wins, so `url=http://host:8080/p?a=b` and `time: 12:30:45` stay whole; keys trimmed, empty and control-character keys rejected, escapes never decoded in keys.
- **Values**: quoted only when the first non-blank char is a quote; closing quote on the same line, only whitespace/comment after it; inline comments cut at `;`/`#` only when preceded by whitespace (so `a;b`, `url#frag` survive); per-carrier escape table exactly as in `specs/ini.md` (unknown sequences keep their backslash, so `C:\Program Files` is intact); continuation decided on **raw** trailing-backslash runs (odd = marker, even = literals), joined verbatim, marker at EOF is an error, continuation lines contribute text not syntax.
- **print**: every value double-quoted with `\\ \" \n \r \t` escaped; section names plain or quote-wrapped when that is what reads back identically; entries the dialect cannot express are omitted (documented precondition).

**Key decisions**

- **Split inside-out** following the grammar's layering: `#` → `?` → scheme (`:` only before the first `/`) → authority (`//`) → path, so no component is ever guessed.
- **Validation is a per-component allow-list**, not a block-list, with percent-encoding checked in the same loop — so space, `<>`, `\`, `^`, backtick, `{}`, `|`, `"`, control and non-ASCII characters are rejected everywhere, and `[` in a path or `:` in a bare host is rejected by the grammar rather than by a lookup table.
- **Authority = reading rules + validation**: userinfo ends at the last `@`, the port starts at the last `:`, brackets are recognized as `IP-literal` (anything after `]` is an ambiguous authority); ports are `*DIGIT` (empty allowed, no numeric range semantics).
- **IPv6 by counting 16-bit groups**: at most one `::`, 8 groups without it and ≤7 with it, embedded IPv4 tail only as the final group, `dec-octet` leading-zero/255 rules, `%25` zones, IPvFuture `v HEXDIG "." 1*(unreserved/sub-delims/":")`.
- **Resolution transcribed from §5.2/§5.3/§5.2.4 in strict mode** (`http:g` stays `http:g`), with the RFC's own dot-segment loop over a stack buffer; parse keeps dot segments intact, only resolve removes them.
- **Recomposition from presence alone**, so `None` vs `Some("")` survives and `parse(uri.to_string()) == uri` holds.

### Key behaviours implemented
- **Streaming**: nothing assumes one `read` fills a buffer — varints are read byte-by-byte (no over-read possible), fixed values loop from the reached offset, payloads are gathered in ≤4096-byte chunks so a bogus `2^31-1` prefix raises instead of allocating 2 GiB, packed elements decode through a `LimitedReader` window.
- **Varints**: any encoding ≤10 bytes, `80 00` = 0, bits past the 64th dropped (`80×9 7F` = 2⁶³, `80×9 02` = 0), 11th continuation byte = overflow, EOF mid-value = truncation; 32-bit readers take the low 32 bits; writers emit minimal forms.
- **Keys/scalars**: `(field<<3)|wire` both ways, field 0 and wire 6/7 rejected, groups returned; int32/enum sign-extended on write, zigzag for sint, bit-exact float/double via reinterpret, little-endian fixed width.
- **Length-delimited**: prefixes validated as int32 on the *full 64-bit* varint (so `2^32` is rejected, per `specs/protobuf.md`), strict table-3-7 UTF-8 with a leading U+FEFF preserved.
- **Packed/unknown**: empty payload → `[]`, mid-element truncation raises; `read_unknown` skips varint/8/LEN/4 bytes and whole groups (nested, matching end-tag field number), raising for wire 4/6/7.
